findings.title: putBackWrite's promise - every coordinate sent whatever the writer's copy holds - did not hold on Foundry 14.370 for a copy out of step
findings.what_happens: The header says a put-back written while a newer move is on its way reads the old spot in the writer's copy, and that diff: false sends every coordinate it names whatever the copy holds. On 14.370 (L1, 18-19.11.2026) the tier-2 test of that promise failed at a table, and the staged case - the GM's copy set out of step with updateSource, a put-back by update with diff: false, with recursive: false, with both, updateEmbeddedDocuments and move - wrote nothing: the GM's socket emitted x and y, PlayerOne received no write of x and kept the old spot. A fresh copy's control also failed in one probe, so the cause (client, server or movement steps) is not separated.
findings.failure_scenario: A player's illegal crossing is put back by the primary GM while that GM's copy of the token is a step behind; the put-back does not land, and the token stays past the veto on every browser.
findings.expected: A put-back that lands whatever the writer's copy holds, or a guard that reads the server's spot and writes again; held by a test that is green at a table.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that L1's tree had today's putBackWrite (git show 179c2644:scripts/movement.mjs:3493-3495, identical). Looked for a second write or a read-back after putBackWrite in sendBack and handleSendback: none named in R7741's census. The staged copy (updateSource) is artificial and one fresh-copy control failed too, so whether the race occurs in play, and why the server did not apply the write, stay open (not_established).

l1.settles_if: lands: the finding falls to the staged case; stays past the veto: the finding is confirmed in play

findings.title: A Truth Bullet's put-back writes null for a guarded flag the bullet never had, so a key world-secrets.mjs forbids (remnantRef) comes back, empty
findings.what_happens: The guard records every guarded flag as `getFlag(...) ?? null`, remnantRef among them; the put-back writes the guard's value for each path the player touched. A player's console write of remnantRef on their own bullet (or of the module's flags whole, which touches every guarded path) is put back as remnantRef: null, not as no key. world-secrets.mjs names a null remnantRef on an Item as a world secret, so checkState and the canary would name it. No secret is in it. E40's paper named this and asked the owner; it is still so on b5a29e73.
findings.failure_scenario: A player writes remnantRef onto their bullet from the console; the primary GM puts it back as remnantRef: null, and at the next start the GM's console warns of a world secret on that item though nothing secret is in it.
findings.expected: A put-back of a field that was absent removes it (forcedDeletion() or unsetFlag), as the paper's question proposes.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a later cleaner: liftBulletRefs (truth-bullets.mjs:1940) would take it off but runs once as the migration clause liftBulletRefs (migrate.mjs:788, since 1.2.64), not again. Looked for a test pinning null: none found by grep of remnantRef in the put-back tests. The owner's answer to the paper's question was not found in docs/dev/e40 or the release notes.
